chunks: From him, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) read to me the sheet of the Book of Inheritance (al-Fara'id), which is the dictation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand.
And within it is: 'That the shares (of inheritance) do not increase (beyond the fixed portions).'
ai.seo_question: What does the principle 'al-sihham la ta'ul' mean in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the Shia doctrine of 'al-sihham la ta'ul,' asserting that fixed Quranic shares remain constant and do not expand to consume the entire estate, a view rooted in a authoritative *sahifa* dictated by the Prophet and penned by Ali ibn Abi Talib. This distinction highlights the Shia interpretation of divine legislative intent, preserving the integrity of specific heirs' portions against total absorption by other claimants. The attribution to Ali’s handwriting further emphasizes the continuity of prophetic knowledge through the Ahl al-Bayt in matters of inheritance law.
